deviations.what: T028's three acceptance scenarios (component override, page-template override, no-view/no-query) are covered by two tests rather than a literal one-per-scenario split, and scenario 1 is proved by rendering the component directly rather than through a Plans-page HTTP request.
deviations.why: Both override templates live in the same tests/project_app application, matching this repo's one-app override pattern (tests/settings_with_project_template_override.py) instead of a second settings module. With both templates present at once, any HTTP request to the shipped Plans page URL always resolves the project's own plans.html first, so a scenario-1 test built as 'request the Plans page with only the component overridden' is unreachable without either a second settings module (which the brief rules out as an invented mechanism) or committing the page override separately from the component override (which the brief also rules out — both are meant to be added to the existing project app). Rendering the component directly with RequestFactory sidesteps the conflict and is also the more literal proof of scenario 3's 'no view' requirement, since it dispatches through no URL and no view at all.

deviations.what: T031's README edit also corrects the sentence immediately before the new link, which claimed the plans page 'do[es] not show anything yet' — narrower than 'just add the link' but inside the same paragraph.
deviations.why: That claim is now false: this story is what makes the plans page show something. Left as written it would have directly contradicted the new link's own caption in the same paragraph. The correction narrows the remaining not-yet-built claim to the billing page, which is still accurate. The README's ## Status section, a few lines above and outside this paragraph, carries the same stale claim and was left untouched — see concerns.
